history.heading: Ancient Persia
paragraphs: Iran is home to one of the world's oldest continuous civilisations. The Elamite civilisation flourished in the southwest from the 4th millennium BCE. In 550 BCE Cyrus the Great founded the Achaemenid Empire, the largest the world had seen, stretching from Egypt and Greece to India. The Cyrus Cylinder is sometimes described as an early charter of rights, and Persepolis was its ceremonial capital.

After Alexander the Great's conquest, the Parthian and then Sasanian empires (224–651 CE) were great rivals of Rome and Byzantium. Zoroastrianism, one of the oldest monotheistic religions, was the state religion.

history.heading: Islamic Iran
paragraphs: Arab armies conquered Persia in the 7th century, bringing Islam. Persian culture remained strong: the poet Ferdowsi wrote the epic Shahnameh, and Persian scholars such as Avicenna (Ibn Sina) and Al-Khwarizmi made major contributions to science, medicine and mathematics.

After Seljuk and Mongol rule, the Safavid dynasty in 1501 made Shia Islam the state religion, shaping Iran's identity, and built the splendid capital of Isfahan. The Qajar dynasty (1789–1925) lost territory to Russia and faced British and Russian influence. The Constitutional Revolution of 1905–11 established a parliament.

history.heading: The Pahlavis and the revolution
paragraphs: Reza Shah Pahlavi took power in 1925 and modernised the country. In 1953 a coup backed by the US and Britain overthrew Prime Minister Mohammad Mossadegh, who had nationalised the oil industry, strengthening Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi's rule. He pursued Westernisation but ruled autocratically.

The 1979 Islamic Revolution overthrew the monarchy, and Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini established the Islamic Republic. US embassy staff were held hostage for 444 days. Iraq invaded in 1980, beginning an eight-year war that killed hundreds of thousands.

history.heading: The Islamic Republic
paragraphs: Ali Khamenei became Supreme Leader in 1989. Reformist and conservative factions have competed within the system. Protest movements, including the 2009 Green Movement and the 2022 "Woman, Life, Freedom" protests after the death of Mahsa Amini in custody, were suppressed.

Iran's nuclear programme has been a major international issue. A 2015 nuclear deal lifted sanctions, but the US withdrew in 2018. In June 2025 Israel and the United States struck Iranian nuclear and military sites during a 12-day war.

culture.heading: Language and religion
paragraphs: Persian (Farsi) is the official language, and Iran is ethnically diverse, with Azerbaijanis, Kurds, Lurs, Arabs, Baloch and others. Most Iranians are Shia Muslims; there are Sunni, Christian, Jewish, Zoroastrian and Baháʼí minorities, the latter facing persecution.

culture.heading: Poetry and arts
paragraphs: Poetry is central to Iranian culture: Hafez, Saadi, Rumi and Omar Khayyam are revered, and verses are often quoted in daily life. Persian carpets, miniature painting, calligraphy and tilework are world famous. Iranian cinema, with directors such as Abbas Kiarostami and Asghar Farhadi, has won international acclaim.
Nowruz, the Persian New Year at the spring equinox, is the most important celebration. Iranian cuisine includes saffron rice, kebabs, and stews (khoresh) such as ghormeh sabzi and fesenjan.

politics.heading: Islamic Republic
paragraphs: Iran is a theocratic republic. The Supreme Leader, a senior cleric, holds ultimate authority over the military, judiciary and state media. The president, elected every four years, leads the government, and the Majlis (parliament) is also elected, but the Guardian Council vets candidates and laws.
The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps is a powerful military, political and economic force. Human rights groups report a high number of executions and restrictions on women, minorities and dissent.

politics.heading: Foreign relations
paragraphs: Iran is hostile to Israel and the United States and has supported allied groups across the region, such as Hezbollah in Lebanon, the Houthis in Yemen and militias in Iraq. This network was weakened in 2024–25, notably by the fall of Bashar al-Assad in Syria. Iran has close ties with Russia and China.

economy.heading: Oil and sanctions
paragraphs: Iran has some of the world's largest oil and natural gas reserves. Oil exports, mainly to China, are vital, though restricted by sanctions. The economy also includes petrochemicals, steel, cars, agriculture (pistachios, saffron and dates) and a large state and quasi-state sector.

International sanctions, mismanagement and corruption have caused high inflation, a sharp fall in the value of the rial, unemployment and emigration of skilled workers. Energy and water shortages have become severe.
